findings: Market is dominated by a few brands: Maruti and Hyundai make up 51.7% of 15,240 listings.
Petrol and diesel cars account for 97.7% of listings; CNG, LPG and Electric are rare.
Prices are strongly right-skewed: median = 5.59 lakh vs mean = 7.75 lakh (skewness 10.1), pulled up by luxury cars.
Automatic cars have a median price 2.1x that of manual cars (10.50 vs 5.00 lakh).
max_power is the feature most strongly correlated with price (r = 0.75), followed by engine size (r = 0.59).
Vehicle age has a modest negative relationship with price (Pearson r = -0.24, Spearman = -0.48); km_driven is weaker still (Spearman = -0.17).
Luxury brands lead on average price: Land Rover, BMW, Jaguar (averages of 38.5, 26.9, 26.5 lakh).
Mileage correlates negatively with price (r = -0.31) likely partly because powerful, expensive cars burn more fuel (mileage vs max_power r = -0.53) - this is association, not cause.
limitations: Asking prices from one platform (CarDekho), not final transaction prices.
No city, condition, accident history or trim-level information, so price drivers are only partly captured.
Only 4 electric and 44 LPG cars - no reliable conclusions can be drawn about them.
Correlation does not prove causation; features such as engine size and power are themselves related.
Dataset has no listing date; vehicle_age is relative to the scrape date.
